name: Sayan Mitra
title: Professor; John Bardeen Faculty Scholar; Director, Center for Autonomy
department: Electrical and Computer Engineering; affiliate Computer Science
fitReason: Current learned perception directly closes the feedback loop on a physical quadrotor, alongside generative policy and formal-safety research. Strong fit for reliable learning-enabled autonomous systems.

physicalEvidence.summary: June 29, 2026 FalconTrack describes an actual custom quadrotor with NVIDIA Jetson Orin, Betaflight and RGB camera. A synthetic-data-trained multi-head perception model feeds an EKF and pose-based visual servo controller; the onboard closed loop runs about 25 Hz. Real flights track a human-driven F1-tenth vehicle and a manually moved gate across two environments, with motion capture used for offline logging/evaluation rather than target feedback to the learned stack. Actual quadrotor-following-quadrotor trials were skipped; those and more aggressive tracking remain simulation-only.
